passages.text: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was the son of Jotham.
Ahaz became king of Judah.
Pekah was the son of Remaliah.
Pekah was king at that time.
Ahaz became king in the seventeenth year of Pekah’s reign.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְפֶ֖קַח בֶּן־ רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בֶּן־ יוֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. And unlike David his father, he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz became king when he was twenty years old.
Ahaz ruled in Jerusalem.
He reigned for sixteen years.
Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
David, his ancestor, did what was right.
Ahaz did not follow David’s example.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר בְּעֵינֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Instead, he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and even sacrificed his son in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz did not follow the LORD his God.
Ahaz did not do what was right.
Ahaz acted like the kings of Israel.
Ahaz walked in their ways.
Ahaz sacrificed his own son in the fire.
This was an evil act.
The nations before Israel did these things.
The LORD drove out those nations because of such abominations.
Ahaz did what those nations had done.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְגַ֤ם אֶת־ בְּנוֹ֙ הֶעֱבִ֣יר בָּאֵ֔שׁ כְּתֹֽעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹרִ֤ישׁ יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king in Jerusalem.
He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
He offered sacrifices on the high places.
He burned incense on the hills.
He burned incense under every green tree.
passages.original: וַיְזַבֵּ֧חַ וַיְקַטֵּ֛ר בַּבָּמ֖וֹת וְעַל־ הַגְּבָע֑וֹת וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־ עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃

passages.text: Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to wage war against Jerusalem. They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
passages.sermon:
Rezin was the king of Aram.
Pekah was the son of Remaliah.
Pekah was the king of Israel.
Rezin and Pekah came to Jerusalem.
They came to fight a war against Jerusalem.
They attacked Ahaz.
They surrounded Ahaz.
They could not defeat Ahaz.
passages.original: אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן־ רְמַלְיָ֧הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיָּצֻ֙רוּ֙ עַל־ אָחָ֔ז וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לְהִלָּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram, drove out the men of Judah, and sent the Edomites into Elath, where they live to this day.
passages.sermon:
Rezin was the king of Aram.
At that time, Rezin took back the city of Elath for Aram.
He forced the men of Judah to leave Elath.
People from Aram came to Elath.
They settled in Elath.
They still live there today.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֤ם אֶת־ אֵילַת֙ לַֽאֲרָ֔ם וַיְנַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת־ הַיְהוּדִ֖ים מֵֽאֵיל֑וֹת וַאֲרַמִּים בָּ֣אוּ אֵילַ֔ת וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hands of the kings of Aram and Israel, who are rising up against me.”
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Tiglath-pileser was king of Assyria.
Ahaz faced attack from Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, king of Israel.
Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser.
Ahaz said to Tiglath-pileser, “I am your servant and your son.”
Ahaz asked Tiglath-pileser to come up and save him.
Ahaz wanted rescue from the king of Aram and the king of Israel.
These two kings were rising up against Ahaz.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אָחָ֜ז מַלְאָכִ֗ים אֶל־ תִּ֠גְלַת פְּלֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַבְדְּךָ֥ וּבִנְךָ֖ אָ֑נִי עֲלֵ֨ה וְהוֹשִׁעֵ֜נִי מִכַּ֣ף מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֗ם וּמִכַּף֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַקּוֹמִ֖ים עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Ahaz also took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king’s palace, and he sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was the king of Judah.
Ahaz took silver and gold from the house of the LORD.
He also took silver and gold from the treasuries of the king’s palace.
Ahaz sent this silver and gold to the king of Assyria as a gift.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אָחָ֜ז אֶת־ הַכֶּ֣סֶף וְאֶת־ הַזָּהָ֗ב הַנִּמְצָא֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וּבְאֹֽצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח לְמֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר שֹֽׁחַד׃

passages.text: So the king of Assyria responded to him, marched up to Damascus, and captured it. He took its people to Kir as captives and put Rezin to death.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria listened to Ahaz.
The king of Assyria marched to Damascus.
The king of Assyria captured Damascus.
He took the people of Damascus away to Kir.
He killed Rezin.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלָיו֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּעַל֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ אַשּׁ֤וּר אֶל־ דַּמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ וַֽיִּתְפְּשֶׂ֔הָ וַיַּגְלֶ֖הָ קִ֑ירָה וְאֶת־ רְצִ֖ין הֵמִֽית׃

passages.text: Then King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria. On seeing the altar in Damascus, King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a model of the altar and complete plans for its construction.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
Tiglath-pileser was the king of Assyria.
King Ahaz went to Damascus.
He went there to meet Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria.
In Damascus, King Ahaz saw an altar.
King Ahaz sent a message to Uriah the priest.
He sent Uriah a model of the altar.
He also sent Uriah complete plans for how to make the altar.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֡ז לִ֠קְרַאת תִּגְלַ֨ת פִּלְאֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ דּוּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּדַמָּ֑שֶׂק וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶל־ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶת־ דְּמ֧וּת הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ וְאֶת־ תַּבְנִית֖וֹ לְכָֽל־ מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

passages.text: And Uriah the priest built the altar according to all the instructions King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and he completed it by the time King Ahaz had returned.
passages.sermon:
Uriah was a priest in Israel.
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
King Ahaz sent instructions from Damascus.
He sent these instructions to Uriah the priest.
Uriah built an altar.
He followed all the instructions King Ahaz sent from Damascus.
Uriah finished building the altar.
He completed the work before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
passages.original: וַיִּ֛בֶן אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז מִדַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן עַד־ בּ֥וֹא הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־ אָחָ֖ז מִדַּמָּֽשֶׂק׃

passages.text: When the king came back from Damascus and saw the altar, he approached it and presented offerings on it.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
King Ahaz saw the new altar.
King Ahaz walked up to the altar.
King Ahaz offered sacrifices on the altar.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ מִדַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרַ֥ב הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וַיַּ֥עַל עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: He offered his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
He returned from Damascus.
He saw the new altar that Uriah the priest had built.
King Ahaz approached the altar.
He offered his burnt offering on the altar.
He offered his grain offering on the altar.
He poured out his drink offering on the altar.
He sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
passages.original: וַיַּקְטֵ֤ר אֶת־ עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ מִנְחָת֔וֹ וַיַּסֵּ֖ךְ אֶת־ נִסְכּ֑וֹ וַיִּזְרֹ֛ק אֶת־ דַּֽם־ הַשְּׁלָמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ ל֖וֹ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: He also took the bronze altar that stood before the LORD from the front of the temple (between the new altar and the house of the LORD) and he put it on the north side of the new altar.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
He saw the bronze altar.
The bronze altar stood before the LORD.
It was in front of the temple.
It stood between the new altar and the house of the LORD.
King Ahaz moved the bronze altar.
He took it away from the front of the temple.
He put the bronze altar on the north side of the new altar.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ת הַמִּזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹשֶׁת֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וַיַּקְרֵ֗ב מֵאֵת֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת מִבֵּין֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וּמִבֵּ֖ין בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹת֛וֹ עַל־ יֶ֥רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ צָפֽוֹנָה׃

passages.text: Then King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, “Offer on the great altar the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, and the king’s burnt offering and grain offering, as well as the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings of all the people of the land. Sprinkle on the altar all the blood of the burnt offerings and sacrifices. But I will use the bronze altar to seek guidance.”
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
Uriah was the priest.
King Ahaz gave a command to Uriah the priest.
He said, “Offer sacrifices on the great altar.
Offer the morning burnt offering on it.
Offer the evening grain offering on it.
Offer my burnt offering on it.
Offer my grain offering on it.
Offer the burnt offerings of all the people of the land on it.
Offer their grain offerings on it.
Offer their drink offerings on it.
Sprinkle all the blood of the burnt offerings on the great altar.
Sprinkle all the blood of the sacrifices on the great altar.
But I will use the bronze altar to seek guidance.”
passages.original: וַיְצַוֵּהוּ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־ אָ֠חָז אֶת־ אוּרִיָּ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן לֵאמֹ֗ר עַ֣ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ הַגָּד֡וֹל הַקְטֵ֣ר אֶת־ עֹֽלַת־ הַבֹּקֶר֩ וְאֶת־ מִנְחַ֨ת הָעֶ֜רֶב וְֽאֶת־ עֹלַ֧ת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְאֶת־ מִנְחָת֗וֹ וְ֠אֵת עֹלַ֞ת כָּל־ עַ֤ם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּמִנְחָתָ֣ם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֔ם וְכָל־ דַּ֥ם עֹלָ֛ה וְכָל־ דַּם־ זֶ֖בַח עָלָ֣יו תִּזְרֹ֑ק וּמִזְבַּ֧ח הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת יִֽהְיֶה־ לִּ֖י לְבַקֵּֽר׃

passages.text: So Uriah the priest did just as King Ahaz had commanded.
passages.sermon:
Uriah was a priest.
King Ahaz gave Uriah commands.
Uriah did everything King Ahaz commanded.
Uriah obeyed King Ahaz completely.
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֑ן כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז׃

passages.text: King Ahaz also cut off the frames of the movable stands and removed the bronze basin from each of them. He took down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone base.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz was the king of Judah.
King Ahaz cut off the frames from the movable stands.
He removed the bronze basin from each stand.
He took down the Sea.
The Sea was a large basin.
The Sea had stood on bronze oxen.
King Ahaz removed the Sea from the bronze oxen.
He put the Sea on a stone base.
passages.original: וַיְקַצֵּץ֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶת־ הַמִּסְגְּר֣וֹת הַמְּכֹנ֗וֹת וַיָּ֤סַר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת הַכִּיֹּ֔ר וְאֶת־ הַיָּ֣ם הוֹרִ֔ד מֵעַ֛ל הַבָּקָ֥ר הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל מַרְצֶ֥פֶת אֲבָנִֽים׃

passages.text: And on account of the king of Assyria, he removed the Sabbath canopy they had built in the temple and closed the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled Judah.
The king of Assyria threatened him.
Ahaz acted because of this threat.
He removed the Sabbath canopy from the temple.
People had built this canopy inside the temple.
He also closed the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ מִיסַךְ הַשַּׁבָּ֜ת אֲשֶׁר־ בָּנ֣וּ בַבַּ֗יִת וְאֶת־ מְב֤וֹא הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַֽחִיצ֔וֹנָה הֵסֵ֖ב בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Ahaz, along with his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled over Judah.
He did many things during his reign.
The rest of the acts of Ahaz are recorded.
His accomplishments are also written down.
These records are in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָחָ֖ז אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz died.
People buried Ahaz with his ancestors.
They buried him in the City of David.
Hezekiah was Ahaz’s son.
Hezekiah became king after Ahaz.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אָחָז֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
